matchups.analysis: Doakes22's looking at a 57% win probability with ESPN projecting a 128.3 finish—that's a 14.6-point cushion over SteelerFan9828's 113.7, and that gap's basically insurmountable when both teams are sitting at zero points heading into their full slate. SteelerFan's got nine starters left (same as Doakes), but Doakes is running Lamar Jackson, Saquon Barkley, and Justin Jefferson—that's the kind of upper-tier talent that turns a projection lead into a straight beatdown when your opponent's banking on Amon-Ra and Joe Burrow to carry the load. The projection gap combined with ESPN's confidence in Doakes's remaining firepower means this is Doakes's to lose unless something catastrophic happens across that entire lineup, which isn't happening when you've got three top-5-at-their-position guys all still pending. SteelerFan would need literally perfect performance from nine guys while Doakes underperforms across the board to pull this off—that's not a comeback scenario, that's just prayer territory.

Both teams are sitting at 0-0 heading into a full Sunday slate, but ESPN's giving kconley5 the slight edge at 53% win probability with a 115.0 projected final versus espnfan7338848211's 109.0—that's a 6-point gap that's basically asking which set of remaining starters actually shows up to play. espnfan's got Ja'Marr Chase, Kenneth Walker, and Drake London left to work with, which should be enough to hang around, but kconley5's got the more complete weapon set with Bijan Robinson, Derrick Henry, and Tee Higgins all still pending—ESPN's basically saying that depth advantage is worth a full touchdown heading into Sunday. This one stays competitive all the way through since both rosters are stacked and neither of you sabotaged yourselves with a brutal start/sit call, but kconley5's projected lead and win probability give them the edge to pull this out if things break even slightly in their favor. Neither team made a meaningful mistake, so whoever gets better games from their skill position guys wins—and right now ESPN's got kconley5 pegged as the more likely side to do that.

82Cole47's walking out with this at 58% win probability and ESPN projecting 128.2 to ESPNFAN6437471416's 112.8—that's a 15.4-point gap that's basically insurmountable when both teams are starting from zero and Cole's got the better remaining talent across the board. Josh Allen, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Rome Odunze should handle the heavy lifting while ESPNFAN's relying on Brock Purdy and a Chase Brown stack to make up ground they don't really have—neither of you sabotaged yourselves, so this is pure roster matchup, and Cole's on the winning side of that equation. ESPNFAN's still got nine starters left to play, so it technically isn't mathematically dead, but ESPN's basically saying you needed a significantly better draft class to compete here, and unfortunately you didn't get one. Cole should coast this one out barring some historically bad performance from his remaining lineup, which at this point would take an act of God given the projection cushion and the talent still pending.

Eric and RGM are basically running in place at 0-0 with ESPN calling this a dead heat at 51-49 win probability, projecting finishes separated by exactly 1.0 point (122.2 to 121.2)—meaning this entire matchup lives or dies on which set of remaining starters actually shows up instead of laying an egg. Both of you managed not to sabotage yourselves with a catastrophic start/sit call, so congratulations on clearing that bar, but now you're just hoping Jonathan Taylor, CeeDee Lamb, and DeVonta Smith (Eric's side) can outlast Christian McCaffrey, De'Von Achane, and Malik Nabers (RGM's side) by a point or two. RGM gets the slightest nod from ESPN's algorithm, but this one's legitimately a coin flip where both rosters are talent-matched enough that it comes down to game script and who doesn't get randomly vultured in the red zone—enjoy Sunday knowing this is going to come down to some ridiculous final-play differential that neither of you controlled.

ESPN88256878's sitting at 52% with a 127.2 projection and has the edge here, but this one's staying tight until the final whistle since ESPNfan83795608's got 122.3 projected and nine starters of their own still pending—that's only a 4.9-point gap that either Puka Nacua or Jaxon Smith-Njigba could evaporate with a decent game. Both rosters are loaded enough that this comes down to execution: ESPN88256878's got Jalen Hurts and Travis Kelce still to go, while ESPNfan's banking on Omarion Hampton and Mike Evans to keep pace, so whoever's skill position guys actually show up on Sunday wins this. ESPN88256878's got the slight projection buffer and win probability edge, but ESPNfan83795608's absolutely got the firepower to flip this—this stays a genuine coin flip until someone's hitting 115+ points while the other stalls out.

Eric and RGM are basically tied right now at 0-0, but ESPN's calling this one for RGM at 51% win probability with a 123.1 final versus Eric's 120.9—that's a 2.2-point gap that could evaporate the second either Jonathan Taylor or Christian McCaffrey decides to show up and actually run the ball. This one's legitimately a coin flip until one of these guys gets to 80 points and the other one stalls out, so enjoy your Sunday afternoon knowing this matchup is getting decided by whichever team's star running back remembers how to football—right now ESPN's giving RGM the edge, but that could flip the second Kyren Williams takes a kickoff return to the house.

ESPN88256878's got the slightly better odds and the deeper bench with nine starters still to play including Jalen Hurts and Travis Kelce, while ESPNfan's matching that firepower with Jayden Daniels and Mike Evans, so this is legitimately anyone's game at this point. Both teams somehow managed not to completely sabotage themselves in the process, which is honestly the bare minimum when you're sitting at zero points heading into Sunday's slate, so congratulations on clearing that low bar. ESPN88256878's got a microscopic edge based purely on ESPN's math, but ESPNfan83795608's got enough talent remaining to absolutely flip this if Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Bucky Irving show up—this one stays a coinflip until the final whistle, which beats watching either of you completely implode with a catastrophic start/sit call like you normally do.

Doakes22's completely cooked at 91.1 with a 0% win probability, getting absolutely demolished by espnfan7338848211's 115.9 final—that's a 24.8-point gap that ESPN basically called before Doakes22's last starter even hit the field. The real catastrophe is benching TreVeyon Henderson (13.6) to start Saquon Barkley's embarrassing 3.0-point performance, a 10.6-point swing that turned this into a blowout instead of something remotely competitive when you were already getting stomped. Saquon projecting 17.6 and delivering 3.0 is bad enough, but making that start/sit call yourself and then watching Henderson put up 13.6 on your bench is the kind of decision that lives rent-free in your head all offseason—meanwhile espnfan's Ja'Marr Chase went 26.5 (projected 19.0) while you were busy self-sabotaging with your running back. This one's been dead since Sunday morning kickoff.

SteelerFan9828's completely cooked at 93.9 with a 0% win probability—this one was dead the moment you benched George Kittle's 18.0 points to start Colston Loveland's 1.3-point catastrophe, a 16.7-point swing that turned what could've been competitive into a full blowout before either guy took another snap. Caleb Williams finishing at 7.7 when ESPN had him at 19.4 is rough, but that's almost secondary to the fact that you made one of the worst start/sit calls of the week and then compounded it by having your QB also underperform by 11.7 points—that's basically two separate ways you sabotaged yourself before kickoff even mattered. 82Cole47's running away at 135.4 with 100% win probability and everyone already locked in, meaning Josh Allen's 18-point beat on projection was the exclamation point on a matchup that stopped being competitive the second you decided Loveland was the move over a tight end who actually caught footballs. You got absolutely punished for one decision you had full control over, and that's the kind of thing that's going to sting every time you look at the scoring summary this week.
